queries.sql: SELECT sum(o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders o JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2026-03-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-04-01' AND oi.quantity > 2
queries.why: Benchmark h09 trap: orders.shipping_fee repeated once per matching order item (order_items.order_id is not unique).

queries.sql: SELECT o.status, avg(o.shipping_fee) AS avg_fee FROM sales.orders AS o INNER JOIN sales.order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.status
queries.why: AVG of an order column weighted by item count.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(i.amount) FROM finance.invoices i JOIN finance.payments p ON p.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
queries.why: payments.invoice_id is not unique by schema; labelled by keys (data-dependent: seed data happens to have one payment per invoice).

queries.sql: SELECT c.region, count(c.customer_id) FROM sales.customers c JOIN sales.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.region
queries.why: COUNT(col) on the customers side repeated per order.

queries.sql: SELECT count(a.tier) FROM crm.accounts a JOIN crm.opportunities op ON op.account_id = a.account_id
queries.why: COUNT(a.tier) repeated per opportunity.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(i.amount) AS invoiced FROM finance.invoices i JOIN finance.revenue_entries re ON re.invoice_id = i.invoice_id WHERE re.booked_on >= '2026-01-01'
queries.why: revenue_entries.invoice_id is not unique by schema (data-dependent: seed has one entry per invoice).

queries.sql: SELECT o.status, sum(o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders o LEFT JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.status
queries.why: LEFT JOIN still repeats order rows per item.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(s.mrr) FROM crm.subscriptions s JOIN crm.contacts c ON c.account_id = s.account_id
queries.why: Many-to-many through account_id: subscriptions repeated per contact.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(op.amount) FROM crm.opportunities op JOIN crm.notes n ON n.account_id = op.account_id
queries.why: Opportunities repeated per note on the account.

queries.sql: SELECT avg(p.unit_price) FROM sales.products p JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
queries.why: Product price weighted by items sold.

queries.sql: SELECT count(s.session_id) FROM events.sessions s JOIN events.clicks k ON k.session_id = s.session_id
queries.why: Sessions repeated per click (no rows in seed: labelled by keys).

queries.sql: WITH big AS (SELECT order_id, shipping_fee FROM sales.orders WHERE status = 'paid') SELECT sum(b.shipping_fee) FROM big b JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = b.order_id
queries.why: CTE is a plain filter of orders; still repeated per item.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(x.shipping_fee) FROM (SELECT order_id, shipping_fee FROM sales.orders WHERE status = 'paid') x JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = x.order_id
queries.why: Derived table without aggregation keeps order rows; repeated per item.

queries.sql: SELECT c.region, sum(o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.customers c JOIN sales.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.region
queries.why: Orders joined to items downstream of customers.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(i.amount) FROM finance.invoices i JOIN sales.customers c ON c.customer_id = i.customer_id JOIN sales.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
queries.why: Invoice->customer is N:1, but customer->orders is 1:N, so invoices repeat per order.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders JOIN sales.order_items USING (order_id)
queries.why: Unqualified column and USING join; shipping_fee belongs to orders.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(amount) FROM finance.invoices JOIN finance.payments USING (invoice_id)
queries.why: USING join, unqualified amount belongs to invoices; payments.invoice_id not unique (data-dependent).

queries.sql: SELECT avg(oi.unit_price) FROM sales.order_items oi JOIN sales.returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id
queries.why: returns.order_item_id is not unique; an item can be returned several times (data-dependent in seed).

queries.sql: SELECT sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) FROM sales.order_items oi JOIN sales.returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id
queries.why: Aggregated expression over item columns; returns not unique per item (data-dependent).

queries.sql: SELECT a.tier, count(a.account_id) FROM crm.accounts a LEFT JOIN crm.contacts c ON c.account_id = a.account_id GROUP BY a.tier
queries.why: Classic wrong count: accounts repeated per contact.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(CASE WHEN o.status = 'paid' THEN o.shipping_fee ELSE 0 END) FROM sales.orders o JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
queries.why: Aggregate over CASE of an orders column.

queries.sql: SELECT round(sum(o.shipping_fee), 2) AS fees FROM sales.orders o JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
queries.why: Aggregate wrapped in a function.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(o.shipping_fee) / count(*) FROM sales.orders o JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
queries.why: SUM(o.shipping_fee) still fans out even though COUNT(*) does not count.

queries.sql: SELECT avg(i.amount) FROM finance.invoices i JOIN finance.revenue_entries re ON re.invoice_id = i.invoice_id JOIN finance.payments p ON p.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
queries.why: Invoices joined to two non-unique children (data-dependent in seed).

queries.sql: SELECT sum(s.mrr) FROM crm.subscriptions s JOIN crm.accounts a ON a.account_id = s.account_id JOIN crm.opportunities op ON op.account_id = a.account_id
queries.why: Subscription->account N:1 safe, account->opportunities 1:N repeats subscriptions.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(op.amount) FROM crm.accounts a JOIN crm.opportunities op ON op.account_id = a.account_id JOIN crm.subscriptions s ON s.account_id = a.account_id WHERE s.status = 'active'
queries.why: Opportunities repeated per active subscription of the same account.

queries.sql: SELECT o.customer_id, sum(o.shipping_fee) AS fees FROM sales.orders o JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.customer_id HAVING sum(o.shipping_fee) > 100
queries.why: Fan-out in both select and HAVING.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders o, sales.order_items oi WHERE oi.order_id = o.order_id AND oi.quantity > 1
queries.why: Implicit comma join with equality in WHERE.

queries.sql: SELECT p.category, sum(p.unit_price) FROM sales.products p JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN sales.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY p.category
queries.why: Many-to-many through the order_items bridge: product price repeated per sale.

queries.sql: SELECT count(c.region) FROM sales.customers c JOIN events.sessions s ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id
queries.why: Customers repeated per session (no sessions in seed: labelled by keys).

queries.sql: SELECT count(c.full_name) FROM sales.customers c JOIN finance.invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id
queries.why: Customers repeated per invoice.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(re.amount) FROM finance.revenue_entries re JOIN finance.payments p ON p.invoice_id = re.invoice_id
queries.why: Join on invoice_id, non-unique on both sides by schema (data-dependent: unique in seed).

queries.sql: WITH items AS (SELECT order_id, quantity FROM sales.order_items) SELECT sum(o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders o JOIN items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
queries.why: CTE is an unaggregated projection of order_items; non-unique order_id.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(o.shipping_fee) FILTER (WHERE o.status = 'shipped') FROM sales.orders o JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
queries.why: FILTER does not change the repeated rows.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(s.mrr) FROM crm.subscriptions s JOIN crm.contacts c ON c.account_id = s.account_id AND c.email LIKE '%@example.com'
queries.why: Equality on non-unique account_id plus a filter.

queries.sql: SELECT avg(a.quantity) FROM sales.order_items a JOIN sales.order_items b ON b.order_id = a.order_id AND b.order_item_id <> a.order_item_id
queries.why: Self join on non-unique order_id repeats each item per sibling.

queries.sql: SELECT SUM("o"."shipping_fee") FROM "sales"."orders" AS "o" JOIN "sales"."order_items" AS "oi" ON "oi"."order_id" = "o"."order_id"
queries.why: Quoted identifiers, same shape as h09.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.order_items oi RIGHT JOIN sales.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
queries.why: RIGHT JOIN with orders as the preserved side; repeated per item.

queries.sql: select c.customer_id, count(c.region) as n from sales.customers as c join sales.orders as o on c.customer_id = o.customer_id join sales.order_items as oi on oi.order_id = o.order_id group by c.customer_id
queries.why: Lowercase SQL; customers repeated per order and item.

queries.sql: SELECT tier, sum(mrr) FROM crm.accounts a JOIN crm.subscriptions s ON s.account_id = a.account_id JOIN crm.contacts c ON c.account_id = a.account_id GROUP BY tier
queries.why: Unqualified tier and mrr; subscriptions repeated per contact.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders o WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2026-03-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-04-01' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sales.order_items oi WHERE oi.order_id = o.order_id AND oi.quantity > 2)
queries.why: EXISTS semi-join: each order counted once.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) FROM sales.order_items oi JOIN sales.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'paid'
queries.why: order_items -> orders is N:1 on orders' primary key; item rows not repeated.

queries.sql: SELECT p.category, sum(oi.quantity) FROM sales.order_items oi JOIN sales.products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category
queries.why: Join to products primary key.

queries.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM sales.orders o JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
queries.why: COUNT(*) never counts.

queries.sql: SELECT max(o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders o JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
queries.why: MAX is not affected by repetition.

queries.sql: SELECT min(i.issued_on), max(i.issued_on) FROM finance.invoices i JOIN finance.payments p ON p.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
queries.why: MIN/MAX never count.

queries.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT o.order_id) FROM sales.orders o JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE oi.quantity > 2
queries.why: COUNT(DISTINCT) is immune to repetition.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(DISTINCT o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders o JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
queries.why: DISTINCT aggregates are excluded by the definition (semantically dubious, but not a fan-out).

queries.sql: SELECT sum(o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders o JOIN (SELECT order_id, sum(quantity) AS qty FROM sales.order_items GROUP BY order_id) x ON x.order_id = o.order_id
queries.why: Join target grouped by order_id, so unique.

queries.sql: WITH q AS (SELECT order_id, sum(quantity) AS qty FROM sales.order_items GROUP BY order_id) SELECT sum(o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders o JOIN q ON q.order_id = o.order_id WHERE q.qty > 5
queries.why: Pre-aggregated CTE is unique on order_id.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders WHERE order_id IN (SELECT order_id FROM sales.order_items WHERE quantity > 2)
queries.why: IN semi-join.

queries.sql: SELECT c.region, sum(oi.quantity) FROM sales.order_items oi JOIN sales.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN sales.customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.region
queries.why: Chain of N:1 joins to primary keys.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(s.mrr) FROM crm.subscriptions s JOIN crm.accounts a ON a.account_id = s.account_id WHERE a.tier = 'gold'
queries.why: N:1 to accounts primary key.

queries.sql: SELECT c.region, sum(i.amount) FROM finance.invoices i JOIN sales.customers c ON c.customer_id = i.customer_id GROUP BY c.region
queries.why: N:1 to customers primary key.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders o JOIN sales.order_status_history h ON h.order_id = o.order_id
queries.why: order_status_history.order_id is its primary key.

queries.sql: SELECT seg.segment, count(a.account_id) FROM crm.accounts a JOIN crm.account_segments seg ON seg.account_id = a.account_id GROUP BY seg.segment
queries.why: account_segments.account_id is its primary key (1:1).

queries.sql: SELECT count(c.customer_id) FROM sales.customers c JOIN crm.accounts a ON a.customer_id = c.customer_id
queries.why: accounts.customer_id carries a UNIQUE constraint, so customers are not repeated.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(c.customer_id) FROM sales.customers c JOIN crm.accounts a ON a.customer_id = c.customer_id
queries.why: Sum of a key-side column where the join column on the other side is unique.

queries.sql: SELECT a.tier, sum(op.amount) FROM crm.opportunities op JOIN crm.accounts a ON a.account_id = op.account_id GROUP BY a.tier
queries.why: Aggregating the many side.

queries.sql: WITH f AS (SELECT customer_id, sum(shipping_fee) AS fee FROM sales.orders GROUP BY customer_id), v AS (SELECT customer_id, sum(amount) AS amt FROM finance.invoices GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT sum(f.fee), sum(v.amt) FROM f JOIN v ON v.customer_id = f.customer_id
queries.why: Both sides pre-aggregated to one row per customer.

queries.sql: SELECT o.status, sum(oi.quantity) FROM sales.orders o LEFT JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.status
queries.why: Aggregated column is on the many side; items are not repeated.

queries.sql: SELECT c.region, sum(p.paid_amount) FROM finance.payments p JOIN finance.invoices i ON i.invoice_id = p.invoice_id JOIN sales.customers c ON c.customer_id = i.customer_id GROUP BY c.region
queries.why: N:1 chain from payments.

queries.sql: SELECT count(r.return_id) FROM sales.returns r JOIN sales.order_items oi ON oi.order_item_id = r.order_item_id JOIN sales.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
queries.why: N:1 chain from returns.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders WHERE status = 'paid'
queries.why: No join.

queries.sql: SELECT customer_id, avg(amount) FROM finance.invoices GROUP BY customer_id
queries.why: No join.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(i.amount) FROM finance.invoices i WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM finance.payments p WHERE p.invoice_id = i.invoice_id)
queries.why: EXISTS semi-join.

queries.sql: SELECT o.order_id, (SELECT sum(oi.quantity) FROM sales.order_items oi WHERE oi.order_id = o.order_id) AS qty FROM sales.orders o
queries.why: Correlated scalar subquery, no join.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders o JOIN LATERAL (SELECT sum(oi.quantity) AS qty FROM sales.order_items oi WHERE oi.order_id = o.order_id) x ON true
queries.why: Lateral aggregate returns exactly one row per order (and the join is not on columns).

queries.sql: SELECT sum(fx.rate) FROM finance.fx_rates fx JOIN finance.currencies c ON c.code = fx.currency
queries.why: N:1 to currencies primary key.

queries.sql: SELECT c.region, sum(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) FROM sales.order_items oi JOIN sales.products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN sales.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN sales.customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.region
queries.why: Every join lands on a primary key.

queries.sql: SELECT count(k.click_id) FROM events.clicks k JOIN events.sessions s ON s.session_id = k.session_id
queries.why: N:1 to sessions primary key.

queries.sql: SELECT count(ref.referral_id) FROM events.signup_referrals ref JOIN events.signups s ON s.signup_id = ref.signup_id
queries.why: N:1 to signups primary key.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders UNION ALL SELECT sum(amount) FROM finance.invoices
queries.why: No joins.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(oi.quantity) FROM sales.order_items oi WHERE oi.order_id IN (SELECT order_id FROM sales.orders WHERE status = 'paid')
queries.why: IN semi-join on the aggregated table.

queries.sql: WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT order_id FROM sales.order_items WHERE quantity > 2) SELECT sum(o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders o JOIN d ON d.order_id = o.order_id
queries.why: SELECT DISTINCT order_id makes the CTE unique on order_id.

queries.sql: WITH big AS (SELECT order_id FROM sales.order_items GROUP BY order_id HAVING sum(quantity) > 5) SELECT sum(o.shipping_fee) FROM sales.orders o JOIN big ON big.order_id = o.order_id
queries.why: GROUP BY order_id CTE is unique on order_id.

queries.sql: SELECT avg(DISTINCT i.amount) FROM finance.invoices i JOIN finance.payments p ON p.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
queries.why: DISTINCT aggregate.

queries.sql: SELECT c.region, max(o.ordered_at) FROM sales.customers c JOIN sales.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.region
queries.why: MAX.

queries.sql: SELECT seg.segment, sum(s.mrr) FROM crm.subscriptions s JOIN crm.account_segments seg ON seg.account_id = s.account_id GROUP BY seg.segment
queries.why: account_segments.account_id is a primary key, so subscriptions are not repeated.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(op.amount) FROM crm.opportunities op JOIN crm.accounts a ON a.account_id = op.account_id JOIN crm.account_segments seg ON seg.account_id = a.account_id
queries.why: Chain of N:1 and 1:1 joins.

queries.sql: SELECT sum(oi.quantity) FROM sales.order_items oi JOIN sales.order_status_history h ON h.order_id = oi.order_id
queries.why: history.order_id is its primary key; aggregating the many side.

queries.sql: SELECT count(c.customer_id) FROM sales.customers c JOIN crm.accounts a ON a.customer_id = c.customer_id LEFT JOIN crm.account_segments seg ON seg.account_id = a.account_id
queries.why: Unique customer_id on accounts, primary key on segments.

queries.sql: SELECT a.tier, count(*) FROM crm.accounts a JOIN crm.contacts c ON c.account_id = a.account_id GROUP BY a.tier
queries.why: COUNT(*) never counts.

queries.sql: SELECT a.tier, count(c.contact_id) FROM crm.accounts a JOIN crm.contacts c ON c.account_id = a.account_id GROUP BY a.tier
queries.why: Counts the many-side key; contacts not repeated.
